transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… the main thing is I just can’t seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore, even when it really matters. Like at work, I’ll be tracing a client’s network problem, looking through logs, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve read the same entries three times and I still couldn’t tell you what they said.

And, I mean, I’ve worked with systems for years, so it’s not like I don’t know how to do the job. It’s more like my brain just… slips off the page. Then I’m back at the beginning again, trying to figure out where I lost the thread. That’s what finally made me come in.
Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with focus and attention as a kid or teenager, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it definitely goes back. My mother still brings it up, actually—she’ll kind of laugh and say my grade school report cards were always, “He’s bright, but…” You know, never staying in my seat, blurting out answers before I was supposed to, losing homework even when I’d actually done it.

Which is funny in a way, because I remember having those little folders and trying to keep things neat, and then somehow the paper would just vanish. But yeah, it wasn’t just something that started recently.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

Um… I’m not sure I’d say persistently down, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, but that’s more when I can’t get things done.

Losing interest… I don’t know. I still like the things I like, I think. Although sometimes I’ll sit down to do something and end up on some completely different thing, like I’ll mean to watch one episode of a show and then I’m reading about how the streaming app caches data, which is—sorry, that’s probably not what you meant.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed being sad all the time or not caring about things, not in that way.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—work, health, family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I don’t think so? I mean, I worry about work when something’s going wrong, like if a ticket is sitting there too long or somebody’s server is down, but that feels kind of… tied to an actual thing.

I wouldn’t say I’m just worrying all day about everything for no reason. Although sometimes I’ll start thinking about one problem and then it turns into three other problems, like the way one system dependency leads to another—sorry, that’s probably too much detail. But no, I haven’t really noticed constant worry across work and health and family like that.
These days, do you notice yourself feeling physically restless, needing to move or fidget, or acting or speaking impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah, I do. It’s like… even when I know I’m supposed to just sit still and listen, there’s this kind of motor humming under my skin. Like I need to get up, or check something, or jump to the next problem right that second.

And it’s not always because there’s actually something urgent. It just feels urgent. Like if someone’s explaining something slowly, my brain is already halfway down the hall trying to fix the next thing, and my body wants to follow it.

Besides work, do these focus and restlessness issues also cause problems for you at home or in your personal relationships—like forgetting commitments, losing things, or having trouble following conversations?

Yeah, definitely at home too. I forget ordinary stuff that turns out to be kind of important. Like I’ll mean to return a client’s call—well, that’s work-adjacent, I guess—but it bleeds over. Or I’ll forget to pay the cloud backup bill, and then suddenly I’m getting notices and scrambling.

And there was this volunteer class where I was supposed to bring the right adapter, because of course every projector has a different port now, which is ridiculous honestly, and I brought the wrong one. Then I’m standing there trying to make it work and apologizing to everyone.

So, yeah… it causes problems. I spend a lot of time the next day apologizing and trying to patch whatever I missed.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually elated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts or a surge of energy that was different from your usual self?

I’m not sure I’d call it euphoric or anything like that. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m keyed up and I sleep badly, but it’s usually because something is going on or I’m stuck thinking through a problem.

Several days of feeling like a totally different version of myself, with all this extra energy and not needing sleep… I don’t think so. At least nothing that stands out like that.

I do get irritable sometimes when things are moving too slowly, like if someone is explaining a simple printer issue and it turns into this whole… sorry, that’s not really what you asked. No, I haven’t noticed distinct periods like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong, childhood-onset (per parental report and school records) symptoms of both inattention (losing focus mid-task, forgetting bills/commitments, disorganization, losing items) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (inner restlessness, urge to move, impulsive shifts of attention, blurting answers as a child). Symptoms persist into adulthood, cause functional impairment across multiple settings (work and home/personal relationships), and are not better explained by depression, GAD, or bipolar disorder, which were explicitly screened for and denied. The combined presence of significant inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms meets criteria for ADHD, combined presentation.
